claims.explanation: AM-251 is a CB1/ CB2 receptor antagonist that blocks endocannabinoid signaling; its selective killing likely depends on the presence of functional cannabinoid receptors (CNR1, CNR2) and an intact endocannabinoid system that promotes survival, so lines with high receptor expression or dependence on endocannabinoid-mediated MAPK/ PI3K signaling are sensitized. The virtual cell response (up BCL2, down CDC20, PAK4, HK1) suggests that AM-251 disrupts survival signaling and mitotic/glycolytic programs, consistent with CB1 antagonism in receptor-positive tumors.

features.basis: CB1 receptor is the primary target of AM-251; high expression predicts response
CB2 is also antagonized by AM-251 and mediates antitumor effects in breast cancer
AM-251 targets GPR55, a cannabinoid receptor implicated in cancer signaling
AM-251 targets GPR18, which may contribute to selective effects
AM-251 upregulates BCL2 in virtual cell, suggesting anti-apoptotic buffering reduces killing
AM-251 downregulates CDC20, a mitotic regulator; low CDC20 may impair proliferation and enhance killing
AM-251 downregulates PAK4, a survival kinase; low PAK4 sensitizes to apoptosis
AM-251 downregulates hexokinase 1, disrupting glycolysis and sensitizing cells
CB1 activation induces MAPK; high MAPK signaling may protect against AM-251
AM-251 upregulates MUC1, which can promote survival and reduce drug sensitivity
AM-251 upregulates RELB, an NF-kB subunit that can mediate resistance
TP53 loss may protect from AM-251-induced apoptosis, as virtual cell shows down TP53BP1
